customManagers.description: Bump the biome $schema in the Copier template's biome.jsonc.jinja (customManagers:biomeVersions only reads biome.json/biome.jsonc, and the rendered biome.jsonc in consumer repos is Copier-owned, so it is not tracked there).
Bump the hugoh/hk-config Pkl package pin in the Copier template's hk.pkl.jinja (not caught by hk-config's own .pkl-only customManager)
Bump the jdx/hk pin in the Copier template's hk.pkl.jinja (not caught by hk-config's own .pkl-only customManager)
Bump the jdx/hk pin in the Copier template's mise.toml.jinja (hk-config's manager only matches files named mise.toml, and the built-in mise manager is disabled for hk)

packageRules.description: These pins reach consumers only once go-tools cuts a new tag (go-*.yml via copier update's uses: hash pins, the template's semantic-pr.yml.jinja via its own gh-workflows pin), so force fix (not chore) to make cocogitto's `cog bump --auto` release them. go-tools' own ci.yml and semantic-pr.yml are excluded: they're never consumed externally.
The shared preset disables hugoh/gh-workflows bumps in semantic-pr.yml for consumers (Copier-owned there); go-tools' own copy is the one place Renovate must keep it current.
Same reasoning as above: template/mise.toml.jinja's tool pins only reach consumers via a new go-tools tag.
Same reasoning as above: template/hk.pkl.jinja's and template/mise.toml.jinja's hk-config/jdx-hk pins only reach consumers via a new go-tools tag.

Group non-major bumps to the repo's own mise.toml into one monthly 'dev tools' PR (first weekend of the month) instead of one per tool. npm:renovate keeps its debounce schedule, Go toolchain bumps stay standalone, and golangci-lint stays weekly: it has to be built with a Go at least as new as the code it lints, so a monthly lag would break lint on the next Go bump.

Same for template/mise.toml.jinja, kept a separate group so the batch stays `fix` (per the rule above) and cuts one go-tools release + one copier fan-out a month instead of one per tool. golangci-lint stays weekly, as above.

hk and hk-config bump together in the monthly 'dev tools' PR: an hk-config release can require a newer hk (min_hk_version), which fails CI until the hk bump lands, so they must not arrive separately. They are read by custom managers (the mise manager is disabled for hk), so the dev tools rule above never sees them. 7-day soak for both, so hk-config can't mature before the hk it needs: updates join a branch as each one matures. Mirrors renovate-config's hk/hk-config linters rule, which this repo doesn't extend.
Same for the template's hk.pkl.jinja and mise.toml.jinja pins, in the `fix` 'template dev tools' batch so they cut one go-tools release and one Copier fan-out with the other template tools.

The mise manager looks biome up through github-tags, which finds no updates for it (the tags are @biomejs/biome@<version>), so the pin never moved while the npm-tracked $schema did. Look it up on npm like renovate-config's biome toolchain rule.

go-tools' own biome pin and biome.json $schema move in one PR, so the CLI never lags the schema it validates against, on the same first-weekend window as the dev tools it comes out of (biome is a linter and formatter: a release that adds a rule or reformats code can fail CI). Must stay BELOW the dev tools rule above, whose groupName it replaces.

The same for the template: its pin and $schema reach consumers only through a new go-tools tag, so they move in one `fix` PR (one release, one Copier fan-out). Must stay BELOW the template dev tools rule above.
